job.style: a passage that starts from a common wrong idea and corrects it

passage: Many students mistakenly believe that reproduction is simply about an organism deciding to change or regrow parts to survive. In reality, reproduction is a fundamental biological process ensuring the continuity of life. During asexual reproduction, such as binary fission in Amoeba, the parent cell divides into two daughter cells, meaning the original parent body ceases to exist as a single entity. Unlike the regrowth of a lizard's tail, which is merely repair, true regeneration in organisms like Planaria allows a broken piece to develop into a complete new individual. Furthermore, plants produced through vegetative propagation are clones, meaning they are genetically identical to the parent, not a new variety. In flowering plants, the process is more complex. Pollination is merely the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma, while fertilization is the subsequent fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote. It is a common error to think the pollen grain itself travels down the style; instead, it grows a pollen tube to deliver the male gametes to the ovule. Finally, DNA copying is not a perfect process. Small variations occur naturally during this copying, which are essential for the survival of a species over time, rather than being a conscious choice made by the organism to adapt to its environment.

items.evidence: During asexual reproduction, such as binary fission in Amoeba, the parent cell divides into two daughter cells, meaning the original parent body ceases to exist as a single entity.
items.q: An Amoeba has just finished binary fission. What has happened to the original parent Amoeba?
options: It has become the two new daughter cells
It lives on beside its two daughters
It stays as the larger of the cells
It dies and leaves behind only spores
items.explain: The parent cell divides into two daughter cells, so the original parent body no longer exists as one.

wrong.why: thinks the parent still exists after fission
thinks one daughter is just the old parent
mixes up fission with spore formation

items.evidence: Unlike the regrowth of a lizard's tail, which is merely repair, true regeneration in organisms like Planaria allows a broken piece to develop into a complete new individual.
items.q: Which example shows true regeneration that also makes a new organism?
options: A broken Planaria piece grows into a whole worm
A lizard grows back its lost tail
An Amoeba divides into two daughter cells
A potato piece grows into a new plant
items.explain: A broken piece of Planaria develops into a complete new individual, while a lizard's tail is only repaired.

items.evidence: Furthermore, plants produced through vegetative propagation are clones, meaning they are genetically identical to the parent, not a new variety.
items.q: A gardener grows ten new rose plants from cuttings of one rose. How will they compare with it?
options: They will be genetically identical to it
They will each be a new variety
They will differ because of new gametes
They will differ in every inherited trait
items.explain: Plants from vegetative propagation are clones, genetically identical to the parent and not a new variety.

wrong.why: thinks gametes fuse in cuttings like in fertilization
thinks variation always appears for survival

items.evidence: It is a common error to think the pollen grain itself travels down the style; instead, it grows a pollen tube to deliver the male gametes to the ovule.
items.q: After a pollen grain lands on the stigma, how do male gametes reach the ovule?
options: A tube grows from the pollen grain
The whole pollen grain slides down the style
Insects carry the gametes down to the ovule
The petals pass the gametes to the ovule
items.explain: The pollen grain grows a pollen tube that delivers the male gametes to the ovule.

wrong.why: thinks the pollen grain itself travels down
thinks insects and petals do the whole job
mixes up pollination with later delivery

items.evidence: Small variations occur naturally during this copying, which are essential for the survival of a species over time, rather than being a conscious choice made by the organism to adapt to its environment.
items.q: Why do small variations appear among offspring of the same species?
options: Small changes happen naturally while DNA is copied
The organism chooses changes to suit its surroundings
DNA copying is exact, so changes come from outside
Variations appear only after a disaster strikes
items.explain: Small variations occur naturally during DNA copying, not as a conscious choice made by the organism.

wrong.why: thinks DNA copying is perfectly accurate
thinks variation matters only after disasters
